At Amberley Court School, the safeguarding of our pupils and staff is always our highest priority.
Following recent national concerns regarding the misuse of images taken from school websites and online platforms, we have taken the precautionary decision to temporarily remove staff names and photographs from our website. During this period, some pages may instead use stock images or carefully cropped photographs of learning environments.
We are currently reviewing our website and image-use policy to ensure our online presence continues to reflect both our school community and our commitment to robust safeguarding practices.
We appreciate your patience and understanding while these updates are taking place.
Amberley Court School All Can Shine
At Amberley Court, we create a safe, inclusive space where children and young people feel seen, valued, and supported to thrive socially and academically. We’re a specialist school for pupils aged 6 to 16 with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs).
Every child is welcomed with compassion, met with curiosity, and held within a deep sense of belonging. We understand that behaviour is communication, and we work relationally to build trust, regulation, and confidence, one connection at a time.
Experienced Staff
At Amberley Court, every adult is known as a Coach, because we believe that education is a partnership built on trust, respect, and guidance. Our team brings together skilled professionals from a range of backgrounds in education, therapeutic support, and pastoral care, all united by a shared commitment to compassion, curiosity, and belonging.
We know that strong relationships are the foundation of emotional safety and learning. Whether it’s in the classroom, during a regulation break, or in quiet moments of connection, our Coaches model calm consistency and champion every child’s growth, academically, socially, and emotionally.
Tailored Curriculum
We know many of our pupils have had a tough start in education. That’s why our curriculum is flexible, personalised, and built on strong relationships.
We offer a broad range of subjects alongside life skills, well-being, and therapeutic activities to support social, emotional, and academic development. Pupils can work towards qualifications or follow more practical pathways, depending on their needs.
With small classes and trusted Coaches, we support each child to learn at their own pace, build confidence, and take steady steps forward—so they can grow and shine in their own way.
Supportive Environment
Our school is calm, structured, and designed around the needs of our pupils. With small class sizes, low-stimulus spaces, and access to regulation areas, we help children feel safe and ready to learn. Clear routines, consistent staffing, and therapeutic support create the stability pupils need to build trust, manage emotions, and re-engage with education—at their own pace.

Referrals and Admissions
Amberley Court School is a specialist setting for children and young people aged 6 to 16, all of whom have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Our pupils may be neurodivergent and often have significant Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs. Many have experienced challenges in previous school environments, and our approach is designed to help them feel safe, understood, and ready to re-engage with learning.
Our Admissions Process
Referrals are usually made through a pupil’s local authority, but we also welcome enquiries directly from parents, carers, or other professionals. We currently accept referrals from West Sussex, Brighton & Hove, East Sussex, Hampshire, and surrounding areas.
Once a referral is received, we carefully review whether our school is the right fit for the child’s needs. If so, we invite the young person and their family to visit us, meet our team, and experience the nurturing environment we offer. This is an opportunity to explore our curriculum, ask questions, and get a feel for daily life at Amberley Court.
If everyone agrees that the school is a good match, and the placement is supported by the local authority, we will work closely with all involved to ensure a smooth, supportive transition.

Our Prospectus
Our school prospectus gives you an in-depth look at what life is like at Amberley Court School. It outlines our approach to education, well-being, and support, and includes key information about the curriculum, admissions, therapies, and our values of Compassion, Curiosity and Belonging. We encourage families, carers and professionals to explore it as a first step in understanding how we work with children who may not have felt safe or successful in other settings.
Please ask the school office for a copy of our prospectus.
Local Offer
Amberley Court School forms part of the Local Offer provided by local authorities to support children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Once we are a registered school our entry on the Local Offer will provide a detailed overview of the specialist support we offer, our admission criteria, and how we meet the needs of pupils with EHCPs.
For more information, please visit the Local Offer section of your local authority’s website or get in touch with us directly to discuss whether Amberley Court could be the right setting for your child.

Our Curriculum
At Amberley Court, our curriculum is flexible, supportive, and shaped around the needs of each learner. We focus on creating the right conditions for pupils to re-engage with learning—building confidence, filling in gaps, and celebrating progress every step of the way.
We offer a broad and balanced mix of subjects, with the National Curriculum serving as a framework for our highly bespoke, personalised holistic curriculum. English and Maths remain central to the curriculum at Amberley Court, but just as important is the development of each pupil’s personal, social and emotional skills. We give thoughtful weight to all subject areas, often bringing learning to life through cross-curricular themes and creative experiences.
Learning goes beyond the classroom. Outdoor activities and educational visits are an essential part of our offer, helping to inspire curiosity, build confidence, and support emotional development. Pupils benefit from regular opportunities to take part in swimming, PE, and community-based experiences that enrich both learning and well-being.
We recognise that not all pupils will be ready to access a full National Curriculum straight away. Our curriculum is carefully differentiated to meet individual needs, with the aim of gradually expanding access and providing every child with meaningful learning opportunities that match their readiness and potential.
As pupils grow in confidence, they can work towards recognised qualifications, depending on their needs and interests. Some follow more practical or vocational routes that prepare them for life beyond school.
Because every child is different, our Coaches adapt teaching to suit each pupil’s strengths, interests, and support needs, ensuring they feel safe, seen, and able to succeed.
Learning at Amberley Court isn’t just about academic progress. It’s about helping every child take steady, supported steps forward at their pace, in their way, and with the right people beside them.
Core Subjects
We teach English, Maths and Science in a calm, supportive environment that helps pupils rebuild trust in learning. Small group teaching, clear routines, and individualised support help children make progress at their own pace—filling in gaps, celebrating strengths, and building confidence. When ready, pupils can work towards the qualifications that are right for them.
Personal, Social & Heath Education
PSHE at Amberley Court helps pupils make sense of themselves, others, and the world around them. We explore topics like friendships, feelings, identity, safety, and future choices in ways that are accessible, respectful, and relevant. Our curriculum includes Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), delivered with sensitivity and adapted to the needs and developmental stage of each pupil. The focus is always on emotional wellbeing, healthy relationships, and helping pupils feel confident and informed.
Creative Arts
Art, music and other creative subjects are a core part of our curriculum at Amberley Court. These lessons give pupils space to express themselves, explore new ideas, and take pride in what they create. Creative arts can help reduce anxiety, build confidence, and support emotional well-being, all while developing important skills. Whether it’s painting, drawing, making music or trying something new, pupils are encouraged to experiment, reflect and enjoy the process.
P.E & Outdoor Learning
Movement and time outdoors are essential for wellbeing. Our PE sessions focus on enjoyment, participation, and building physical confidence. Activities are varied and inclusive, supporting regulation, teamwork, and self-esteem.
We also make the most of outdoor spaces to support learning in other subjects and to offer pupils moments of calm, connection, and curiosity. Whether it’s forest school-style sessions, nature walks, or simply fresh air and space to move, outdoor learning plays a key role in helping pupils feel grounded and ready to learn.
Humanities
In History, Geography and RE, we help pupils explore the world and their place in it. Our approach encourages curiosity, discussion, and making meaningful connections to real life. Lessons are adapted to be engaging and accessible, often using practical activities, visual resources, and group work to spark interest.
We focus on helping pupils develop an understanding of people, cultures, places, and events—while also encouraging empathy, critical thinking, and respectful dialogue.
Life Skills
Our life skills curriculum helps pupils prepare for everyday challenges and future independence. We cover practical areas like cooking, budgeting, travel training, and personal care, as well as communication, problem-solving, and teamwork. These sessions build confidence and real-world readiness, tailored to each pupil’s strengths and next steps.
Whether it’s learning to make a meal, manage money, or plan a journey, life skills are taught in meaningful, hands-on ways that help pupils feel capable, supported, and prepared for what comes next.
Curriulum Pathway
Meeting Pupils Where They Are
Every child at Amberley Court arrives with their own experiences, strengths, and challenges. We start by creating a calm, safe space where pupils feel they belong.
At this early stage, we focus on emotional regulation, building trust, and reintroducing the routines of learning. Academic work is gently reintroduced through low-pressure, accessible activities—helping pupils reconnect with learning in a way that feels manageable and meaningful.
“The first step isn’t to push forward, it’s to feel safe enough to begin.”
Building Skills and Confidence
Once pupils feel more settled and secure, we begin to strengthen key academic and personal skills. This includes building confidence in reading, writing, and numeracy, while also developing communication, problem-solving, and emotional understanding.
Learning is highly adaptable—our Coaches tailor lessons to reflect each pupil’s needs, interests, and learning style. Alongside core subjects, we offer creative arts, PSHE, physical education, humanities and life skills, giving pupils the chance to succeed across different areas and experience the joy of learning again.
Progress is celebrated in small steps, helping pupils grow in self-belief and motivation.
“With the right support, every small step becomes a sign of strength.”
Moving Towards Meaningful Outcomes
As pupils grow in confidence and capability, we support them to work towards outcomes that reflect their goals and strengths. For some, this may include recognised qualifications such as Entry Level, Functional Skills, or GCSEs. For others, it may involve a more personalised or practical route focused on independence, well-being, and next steps beyond school.
Our approach isn’t about rushing, it’s about making sure every pupil is ready, supported, and working towards something that matters to them. We review progress regularly across academic, social, and emotional areas to ensure each learner is on a path that’s achievable, relevant, and right for them.
“Success looks different for everyone — what matters is that it’s theirs.”
Curriculum Intent, Implementation and Impact
Our curriculum at Amberley Court is built around three pillars:
Core Values, Core Skills and Core Knowledge
These pillars underpin every aspect of learning. Together, they provide the foundations for academic progress, personal growth and preparation for adulthood. You can read more about how these are embedded across our school in the full curriculum document below.
“A good curriculum builds knowledge, develops character and opens doors to the future.”

Our Learning Environment
“A learning space should feel like an invitation, not a demand.”
Amberley Court School is still in its early stages and so is our physical environment. As we prepare to open our doors in September 2025, we are carefully shaping a space that reflects our values of compassion, curiosity, and belonging.
We’re creating calm, welcoming classrooms designed to reduce anxiety and support focus. Our learning spaces will be flexible and nurturing, with low-stimulation zones, access to regulation resources, and clear visual structure to help pupils feel safe and grounded.
We’re also developing quiet rooms, therapeutic areas, and creative spaces that will support individual and small group work. Outside, we’re working to ensure there is space for movement, fresh air, and time to reset—whether through outdoor learning, play, or simply being in nature.
While the building may still be evolving, our commitment is already clear: to create an environment where every child feels seen, safe, and supported to shine.

Our Mission
At Amberley Court School, we are committed to creating a calm, safe, and inclusive environment where every child is seen, valued, and supported. We recognise that each pupil’s journey is unique, and we provide the consistent relationships, tools, and guidance they need to make meaningful progress, both in learning and in life.
Through a deeply relational and therapeutic approach, we help children develop the skills to regulate, reflect, and reconnect. Our aim is not only to support them in the classroom, but to equip them with the confidence, resilience, and self-awareness they need for the future beyond it.
Our Core Values
Compassion
We meet each other with empathy and patience. We see behaviour as communication and respond with kindness, even in moments of challenge. Compassion extends to pupils, families, and colleagues alike.
We connect before we correct. We lead with understanding.
Curiosity
We look beyond the surface. We ask questions, not to challenge, but to understand. Curiosity helps us see the why behind behaviour, the story behind the struggle, and the potential in every moment.
We stay open, reflective, and always ready to learn; from our pupils, from each other, and from ourselves.
Belonging
We recognise that true inclusion goes beyond presence, it means being seen, accepted, and valued. Every child and adult deserves to feel they matter here.
We are stronger together, and everyone has a place.
Our Vision and Aims
"With compassion, curiosity and belonging, we create the conditions for every pupil to thrive."

Reignite confidence and self-belief
Support emotional regulation and resilience
Prepare pupils for fulfilling, empowered lives

Many of our learners have experienced disrupted education due to unmet needs, repeated exclusions, or long periods out of school. They may arrive with high levels of anxiety, low self-esteem, and a belief that school isn’t a place for them.
We’re here to change that.
At Amberley Court, every pupil is welcomed with compassion, met with
curiosity, and held within a deep sense of belonging. Our team, known as Coaches, are not just educators; they are trusted adults who build strong,
meaningful relationships that support regulation, self-worth, and growth.
We understand that behaviour is communication, and we respond with calm
consistency, emotional attunement, and a trauma-informed approach.
Our curriculum blends academic learning with therapeutic support, practical skills, and emotional literacy. Every child’s journey is personalised and paced around their needs, interests, and goals. Whether it’s learning to read with
confidence, exploring science through hands-on experiences, or taking part in Thrive and wellbeing sessions, we ensure that every child is seen, heard, and
supported to progress.
We know that success looks different for every pupil. That’s why we define achievement not just by qualifications—but by confidence, resilience,
relationships, and the ability to thrive in the world beyond school.
If you're looking for a school where your child will be truly understood,
supported, and inspired to grow—Amberley Court is ready to welcome you.
We’d love to show you around.

Our team
At Amberley Court, every adult is known as a Coach, because we believe in guidance, partnership, and walking alongside our pupils, not leading from above. Our team brings together experienced educators, therapists, and support staff who share a deep commitment to helping every child feel safe, understood, and able to grow.
We work collaboratively, reflecting together, learning from each other, and placing relationships at the heart of everything we do. Through consistent support, curiosity, and compassion, our staff create the trust and stability pupils need to re-engage with learning and build confidence in themselves.
We are trauma-informed, neurodiversity-affirming, and always learning. Whether offering a calm presence, adapting a lesson, or supporting a child through a tough moment, each Coach plays a vital role in helping our pupils shine.
As a new school, we are still growing our team. We are carefully building a staff community that reflects our values and brings the right mix of experience, compassion, and curiosity to support our pupils from day one and beyond.

Our Therapies and Interventions
At Amberley Court, we believe that emotional wellbeing is the foundation for learning. Many of our pupils arrive with past experiences that have impacted their confidence, regulation, and ability to engage in a typical school environment. That’s why therapeutic support is woven through everything we do.
We offer a range of evidence-informed interventions tailored to meet the individual needs of each child. These are delivered through both structured sessions and integrated, everyday practices guided by strong relationships and a trauma-aware approach.
SALT (Speech & Language Therapy)
We work with a specialist to support children who find speaking, understanding, or social communication difficult. SALT sessions help unlock confidence and connection, making friendships, lessons and life feel that bit easier.
Occupational Therapy
Our Occupational Therapist helps pupils who struggle with motor skills, sensory sensitivities or everyday tasks. By understanding how each child experiences their world, we can make school feel more manageable and more comfortable.
Art and Play Therapy
Some feelings are too big—or too hard—to put into words. Art and play therapy give our pupils creative, non-verbal ways to explore their emotions, build confidence, and feel understood.
Sensory Profiles
Many of our pupils experience the world in heightened or unique ways. We create individual sensory profiles to help us tailor spaces, routines, and responses, so that children feel calm, safe, and in control.
THRIVE Approach
Thrive is central to how we support emotional development at Amberley Court. It helps us understand what each child needs to feel safe, connected, and ready to learn using consistent, relationship-based strategies grounded in neuroscience and child development.
EFT (Emotional Freedom Techniques) and Massage
This gentle approach involves tapping on pressure points to help pupils regulate their emotions. It’s a simple, empowering tool that some of our learners find really effective when they're feeling anxious or overwhelmed.
We offer therapeutic massage (always with consent and care) as a calming intervention to support sensory integration, relaxation, and regulation, particularly for children who carry high levels of tension or anxiety in their bodies.
LEGO®-based Therapy
We use LEGO sessions as a way to bring children together through shared tasks. It builds trust, communication and teamwork—especially for those who find verbal interaction tricky or overwhelming.

Headteacher's Message
Dear Parents, Carers, and especially PUPILS,
I am extraordinarily privileged to welcome you to Amberley Court School. Amberley Court School (ACS) is a specialist school for children and young people aged 6 to 16 with high levels of anxiety and Social Emotional Mental Health difficulties. Many of our pupils have faced challenges in previous settings, and we are proud to offer them a place where they feel safe, accepted, and supported. All of the children in our care have a variety of difficulties, whether that be Autism (ASC), ADHD or they may just feel that they struggle to ‘fit in’ and communicate with the world around them, but we are all different. We all have different strengths and weaknesses, but this does notlessen us, it is what makes us unique, interesting and exciting. At ACS we nurture yet challenge every pupil, promoting their strengths and building their confidence, resilience and self-worth, so they SHINE.
At Amberley Court School (ACS), our core belief is that All Can Shine. Every child has unique strengths, and we are committed to helping them discover and develop their potential —academically, socially, and emotionally. Our approach is grounded in our three core values:
Belonging – building a strong, inclusive community where every pupil feels safe and valuedCompassion – showing empathy, kindness, and respect in everything we doCuriosity – encouraging a love of learning and discovery in every form
We understand that many of our pupils arrive with anxiety, low self-esteem, low self-worth and/or negative experiences of education. That’s why relationships, trust, and emotional wellbeing are at the heart of our work. Our highly-skilled and compassionate staff team, all known as ‘coaches’, from the Headteacher to the support staff, endeavour to create a calm, predictable environment, where children feel secure enough to take risks, learn new skills and grow in confidence.
Our curriculum is adapted and personalised, designed to reduce anxiety while promoting engagement, resilience, and independence. We work closely with families, carers, and external professionals, to ensure every child receives the tailored supportthey need to thrive academically as well as holistically.
Amberley Court School is more than just a place of learning — it’s a place of belonging. A place where progress is personal, every voice is heard, and every success is celebrated. Every child will have a THRIVE profile ( www.thriveapproach.com ) that is bespoke in aiding that pupil to engage in all aspects of school life, whilst building skills and coping strategies that will aid them throughout their lives.
If you’d like to find out more, please don’t hesitate to get in touch or arrange a visit. We’d love to hear from you and welcome you into our small, friendly and caring school environment.
Take care,JamesHeadteacherAmberley Court School“All Can Shine”
